Stanislavchyk Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytsia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Stanislavchyk — known successively as Yushkov, then Chagarin after being rebuilt following a Tatar raid, and finally Stanislavchyk under Russian rule — had a Jewish population that reached about a quarter of the town by 1897. Under Soviet rule, one of the town's two synagogues was rededicated as a library in 1929, and the other later became a cinema. Under Romanian administration as part of the Transnistria Governorate, a ghetto here held around 200 local Jews alongside hundreds of deportees from Bukovina and Bessarabia, many of whom died from harsh conditions; 81 remained by September 1943. This cemetery, established in the 18th century, is looked after today by a named local caretaker, Konstantin, who lives across the street.
